exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. PyTorch stable documentation reviewed 2026-09-19 (current docs identified as 2.14).

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; typed recall and coding questions provide the scored retrieval signal.

authoring_notes: This is a practical learning track, not a certification. Domain weights are curriculum emphasis weights used for adaptive selection. Learning placeholders are exact cloze versions of their revealed text. Reviewed against PyTorch 2.14-era official documentation and the app's structured typed-fill code/table renderer on 2026-09-19.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Custom neural networks normally subclass `__________`, call `super().__init__()`, and assign child layers as module attributes.

reveal.text: Custom neural networks normally subclass `nn.Module`, call `super().__init__()`, and assign child layers as module attributes.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Registered child modules and parameters are discovered by methods such as `__________` and `state_dict()`.

reveal.text: Registered child modules and parameters are discovered by methods such as `model.parameters()` and `state_dict()`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Keeping layers only in an ordinary Python container can bypass __________ unless you use containers such as `ModuleList` or `ModuleDict`.

reveal.text: Keeping layers only in an ordinary Python container can bypass module registration unless you use containers such as `ModuleList` or `ModuleDict`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: A Module defines computation in __________, while normal user code should call `model(x)` so Module hooks and wrapper behavior are respected.

reveal.text: A Module defines computation in `forward`, while normal user code should call `model(x)` so Module hooks and wrapper behavior are respected.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Implement `def forward(self, x): ...` and invoke the model with `output = __________`.

reveal.text: Implement `def forward(self, x): ...` and invoke the model with `output = model(x)`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not normally call `__________` directly from training code.

reveal.text: Do not normally call `model.forward(x)` directly from training code.

source_refs.title: `forward` and calling the model — PyTorch documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` applies an affine transformation to the last input dimension.

reveal.text: `nn.Linear(in_features, out_features)` applies an affine transformation to the last input dimension.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: For input shaped `[batch, features]`, `nn.Linear(features, hidden)` returns `__________`.

reveal.text: For input shaped `[batch, features]`, `nn.Linear(features, hidden)` returns `[batch, hidden]`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: The input last dimension must match `__________`.

reveal.text: The input last dimension must match `in_features`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` chains modules in order so each module receives the previous module output.

reveal.text: `nn.Sequential` chains modules in order so each module receives the previous module output.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use it for straightforward feed-forward stacks such as `__________`.

reveal.text: Use it for straightforward feed-forward stacks such as `Linear -> ReLU -> Linear`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Use a __________ when the graph needs branching, multiple inputs, skip connections, or other non-sequential logic.

reveal.text: Use a custom `forward` when the graph needs branching, multiple inputs, skip connections, or other non-sequential logic.

modules.title: Use common layers and reason about shapes

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` applies `max(0, x)`, while activations such as GELU provide alternative nonlinearities used in many modern architectures.

reveal.text: `nn.ReLU` applies `max(0, x)`, while activations such as GELU provide alternative nonlinearities used in many modern architectures.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A typical MLP places an activation __________.

reveal.text: A typical MLP places an activation between Linear layers.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Do not automatically add a probability activation to final logits when the chosen loss already expects __________.

reveal.text: Do not automatically add a probability activation to final logits when the chosen loss already expects raw logits.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `nn.Flatten(__________)` commonly flattens all non-batch dimensions while preserving dimension 0 as the batch axis.

reveal.text: `nn.Flatten(start_dim=1)` commonly flattens all non-batch dimensions while preserving dimension 0 as the batch axis.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: For `[N, C, H, W]`, flattening from dimension 1 produces `__________`.

reveal.text: For `[N, C, H, W]`, flattening from dimension 1 produces `[N, C*H*W]`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Bare reshaping that accidentally folds the __________ into features breaks the sample structure.

reveal.text: Bare reshaping that accidentally folds the batch dimension into features breaks the sample structure.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `nn.Conv2d` expects image-like input with channels in the second dimension for batched tensors: `__________`.

reveal.text: `nn.Conv2d` expects image-like input with channels in the second dimension for batched tensors: `[N, C, H, W]`.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: `nn.Conv2d(in_channels, __________, kernel_size, ...)` controls input channels, learned output channels, and spatial kernel size.

reveal.text: `nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, ...)` controls input channels, learned output channels, and spatial kernel size.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: A common shape error is passing __________ data directly to a Conv2d that expects NCHW.

reveal.text: A common shape error is passing NHWC data directly to a Conv2d that expects NCHW.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` downsamples spatial dimensions by taking local maxima over a window.

reveal.text: `nn.MaxPool2d` downsamples spatial dimensions by taking local maxima over a window.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A common pattern is convolution, activation, then pooling to __________.

reveal.text: A common pattern is convolution, activation, then pooling to reduce spatial resolution.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Pooling changes spatial shape, so later Linear layer input sizes must match the __________.

reveal.text: Pooling changes spatial shape, so later Linear layer input sizes must match the post-pooling dimensions.

modules.title: Use embeddings, normalization, and registered modules

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `nn.Embedding(num_embeddings, embedding_dim)` is a learnable __________ that maps integer indices to embedding vectors.

reveal.text: `nn.Embedding(num_embeddings, embedding_dim)` is a learnable lookup table that maps integer indices to embedding vectors.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: If the input index tensor has shape `[*]`, the output adds an embedding dimension of size `__________`.

reveal.text: If the input index tensor has shape `[*]`, the output adds an embedding dimension of size `embedding_dim`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Embedding inputs are __________, not one-hot floating-point vectors passed to Linear.

reveal.text: Embedding inputs are indices, not one-hot floating-point vectors passed to Linear.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `nn.Dropout(p)` randomly zeroes elements with __________ during training and behaves as an identity transform during evaluation.

reveal.text: `nn.Dropout(p)` randomly zeroes elements with probability `p` during training and behaves as an identity transform during evaluation.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Call `model.train()` for training behavior and `__________` before evaluation so Dropout switches modes correctly.

reveal.text: Call `model.train()` for training behavior and `model.eval()` before evaluation so Dropout switches modes correctly.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Dropout behavior depends on module training mode; __________ alone does not switch Dropout to evaluation behavior.

reveal.text: Dropout behavior depends on module training mode; disabling gradients alone does not switch Dropout to evaluation behavior.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: BatchNorm modules can track running statistics and use training-versus-evaluation mode differently, so __________ matter for inference correctness.

reveal.text: BatchNorm modules can track running statistics and use training-versus-evaluation mode differently, so `train()` and `eval()` matter for inference correctness.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: BatchNorm running statistics are __________ and therefore appear in the module state dictionary.

reveal.text: BatchNorm running statistics are registered buffers and therefore appear in the module state dictionary.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Gradient disabling __________ `model.eval()` because evaluation mode changes module behavior rather than autograd recording.

reveal.text: Gradient disabling does not replace `model.eval()` because evaluation mode changes module behavior rather than autograd recording.

source_refs.title: Batch normalization mode behavior — PyTorch documentation

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` stores a list of child modules while keeping them registered with the parent Module.

reveal.text: `nn.ModuleList` stores a list of child modules while keeping them registered with the parent Module.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Use `ModuleList` when you need __________ over a dynamic number of layers but cannot express the computation as a simple Sequential chain.

reveal.text: Use `ModuleList` when you need list-like iteration over a dynamic number of layers but cannot express the computation as a simple Sequential chain.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: A __________ of layers is not a substitute when you need automatic parameter registration by the parent Module.

reveal.text: A plain Python list of layers is not a substitute when you need automatic parameter registration by the parent Module.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `__________` iterates registered Parameter objects, while `model.state_dict()` returns a mapping of registered parameters and persistent buffers.

reveal.text: `model.parameters()` iterates registered Parameter objects, while `model.state_dict()` returns a mapping of registered parameters and persistent buffers.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Optimizers are commonly constructed with `__________` so they know which tensors to update.

reveal.text: Optimizers are commonly constructed with `model.parameters()` so they know which tensors to update.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: A `state_dict` is data, __________ itself.

reveal.text: A `state_dict` is data, not the Python model architecture itself.
